summary: Rerank results reorder after recent embedding normalization + batching change
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that after last week's runtime change (automatic L2 normalization applied to embeddings + a change to batch windowing), rerank endpoint returns the same top-k set but the ordering of results is inconsistent compared to their previous baseline.

Impact:
- VeritasSearch customers see search result order regressions (business-critical for relevance-sensitive workflows).
- Observed for multiple queries across production dataset; not intermittent poster-child but consistent shift correlating with deployment timestamp.

Environment:
- prod us-east, customer using hosted API keys on self-serve plan.
- Affected pipelines: embeddings produced by openaio/embedding-XL-1024, then fed into redwood-reranker-v2 via the rerank endpoint.

Observed behavior:
- Top-10 documents are the same IDs as baseline in ~85% of queries but rank positions shift (e.g., baseline top-1 drops to position 3).
- Median rerank latency increased by ~12% in the customer's sample window (p50 78ms -> 87ms).
- Cosine similarity scores between query and doc embeddings show slight magnitude differences post-normalization; downstream reranker scoring appears sensitive to these tiny changes.

Expected behavior:
- Applying normalization should preserve ordering for reranker when scoring is invariant to input vector magnitude, or else be documented as a breaking change.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use VeritasSearch test account with sample dataset (customer provided minimal reproducible set).
2) Call embeddings endpoint for the query text using openaio/embedding-XL-1024 at timestamps before and after the 2026-03-09 deploy.
3) Submit those embeddings to rerank endpoint (redwood-reranker-v2) with identical candidate lists and compare ordering and scores.
4) Toggle the normalization flag at the embeddings input stage (simulating pre-deploy behavior) and re-run rerank to observe ordering differences.
steps_to_reproduce: Obtain customer sample queries and candidate document IDs (attached in ticket).
Call /v1/embeddings with model=openaio/embedding-XL-1024 before/after normalization change (or simulate by dividing by norm).
Feed embedding vectors into rerank endpoint with identical candidate list and identical reranker config.
Compare top-k orderings and per-candidate scores; compute Spearman rank correlation between baseline and new ordering.

investigation_notes: 03/10 - Initial triage by CS confirmed customer dataset reproduces ordering shift with prod embeddings.
03/10 - Run local A/B with and without L2 normalization on embeddings: normalization reduced vector magnitude variance and changed cosine scores by ~1-2e-3 in many cases.
03/11 - Reviewed commit history: embeddings library merged automatic normalization flag by default on 2026-03-09 (PR #178).
03/11 - Reranker model expects raw unnormalized embeddings; scoring head includes a learned scale term that magnifies small differences, explaining ordering sensitivity.

03/11 - Batch window change: server-side continuous batching now groups requests up to 12ms by default (commit in re-ranker runtime), causing slight reordering of KV cache warmups and timing-dependent scoring for near-ties.
03/12 - Hypothesis: combined effect of normalization (small score deltas) + altered batching timing (different KV-cache hit pattern) causes reproducible rank shifts for near-tied candidates.
customer_impact_summary: Search relevance ordering regressed for a production customer (VeritasSearch). They report measurable drop in click-through on affected queries and requested rollback or mitigation.
mitigation_attempts: 2026-03-11: Suggested customer-side workaround to L2-denormalize vectors before submitting to rerank (multiply by stored norms) - verified this restores baseline ordering in tests.

2026-03-11: Temporarily increased batch window to 0ms for customer's routed requests to avoid batching timing differences (via per-tenant policy) — reduced p50 latency back near baseline and restored order for most queries.
2026-03-12: Disabled automatic normalization in embeddings service for the customer's traffic as an immediate fix (config flag).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12: Rollback performed for normalization flag on customer-specific route; monitoring shows ordering correlation restored (Spearman rho > 0.98 vs pre-deploy baseline).
2026-03-12: Opened follow-up engineering story to add explicit feature flag and contract for embeddings normalization behavior (INT-3456).
2026-03-12: Long-term plan: update reranker training to be invariant to embedding magnitude or include an explicit preprocessing contract in model catalog docs.
2026-03-12: Notified customer CS/PM with summary and recommended steps for model-compatibility validation during runtime changes.
next_steps: ENG: Add integration test to reranker CI that asserts stable ordering for small-scale normalization perturbations (owner: @diego).
ML: Evaluate re-training reranker with normalized inputs to remove sensitivity (owner: @liao-ml).
DX: Update model catalog docs to clearly indicate whether embeddings are L2-normalized by default and add migration notes (owner: @marie-dx).
OPS: Expose per-tenant batching window policy and document tradeoffs; consider safe default for relevance-sensitive customers.
